get.description:
List all entities in the knowledge graph.

Optionally filter by vertex label (e.g. ``Technology``, ``Person``).

Returns an empty list with ``meta.graph_enabled = false`` when Apache AGE
is not installed.

Get full details for an entity including graph neighbors and related memories.

The memories half must answer, or this is a 503. The graph half may fail
and leave neighbours empty: then ``meta.degraded`` is true and
``meta.degraded_reasons`` says why, so an empty list is not mistaken for
"no neighbours" (audit M20). Without Apache AGE the graph half is not
attempted and ``meta.graph_enabled`` is false, as on the other routes.

Find a connecting path between two entities in the knowledge graph.

Returns ``found: false`` with ``meta.graph_enabled = false`` when Apache
AGE is not installed.

post.description:
Execute a raw Cypher query against the knowledge graph.

**Admin-level endpoint** — allows arbitrary read queries, across every
tenant's graph. Two things are required: an owner API key
(``require_owner_key``; 403 otherwise) and ``X-Tenant-ID: default``. The
header alone is not enough, because any service-key holder can send it.
Write operations (CREATE, SET, DELETE, MERGE, REMOVE, DROP) are blocked.

Returns an empty list with ``meta.graph_enabled = false`` when Apache AGE
is not installed. A malformed query against a working install is still 400.

Run a hybrid search combining graph structure with vector similarity.

The graph narrows entity scope, then vector search refines
by semantic similarity.

get.description:
List memories with optional status, tag, and importance filters.

Supports both offset and cursor-based pagination. When a cursor is
provided, offset is ignored and keyset pagination is used for
consistent performance on large datasets.

post.description:
Create one or more memories.

If the body contains free-form text, it is routed through the
full ingestion pipeline (extraction → importance scoring →
contradiction detection → storage). Otherwise, the memory is
stored directly.
post.summary: Create memories from text or structured input

post.description: Approve/reject memories in batch (distillation review will lean on this).

Fetch several memories by id in one round trip.

The expand half of progressive disclosure. A caller runs recall or search
with ``index_only`` — a compact ``{id, content, tags, score, status}``
line per memory — then comes back here for the few it actually wants.

**This is where surfacing is recorded.** The recall cooldown and the
access count (which feed decay and the ``frequency`` ranking signal) fire
on the expand, not on the index: an index-only recall discloses nothing,
so recording it there would burn a week of cooldown and inflate
``access_count`` on memories nobody read. Full (non-index) recall still
records at recall time, because there the content *is* in the response.

Unknown or other-tenant ids are silently absent from the result rather
than an error — ``meta.requested`` vs ``meta.found`` tells the caller.
post.summary: Expand memory ids to full memories (progressive-disclosure step 2)

get.description: Number of memories awaiting approval for this tenant.

delete.description: Delete a memory and cascade to association tables.

get.description: Retrieve a single memory by its UUID.

patch.description: Apply a partial update to an existing memory.

post.description:
Approve a pending (or rejected) memory — it becomes active/usable.

``confirm_as_owner_fact`` is the one field here that grants authority, so
it is checked against the authenticated ingress and not against anything
in the body: a third party, or an agent posting on behalf of a page it
read, is refused (403) rather than obeyed.

Mark a memory as superseded because the user says it is no longer true.

If a replacement string is provided, creates a new memory that
supersedes the old one (with full provenance chain). The old memory
is kept in the supersession chain for history.
post.summary: Deny a memory — mark as no longer accurate

post.description:
Confirm that a memory is still accurate.

Resets confidence to 0.9, updates last_reinforced timestamp,
and increments the reinforcement counter. Use this when the
system asks "is this still true?" and the user confirms.
post.summary: Reinforce a memory — confirm it is still accurate

post.description: Reject a pending memory — hidden everywhere, re-capture allowed.

Restore an archived memory back to active status.

Changes the memory's status from 'archived' to 'active',
making it available for search and recall again.

Search memories using configurable strategy.

Modes:
- ``vector``: Pure cosine similarity (fastest, semantic only)
- ``hybrid``: Vector + BM25 keyword matching (default, best balance)
- ``tri_hybrid``: Vector + BM25 + graph entity proximity (most comprehensive)
post.summary: Search across memories (vector, hybrid, or tri-hybrid)

post.description:
Ask a natural language question and get a synthesized answer.

Runs semantic search, then passes results to the LLM for synthesis.
post.summary: Ask a question — get a synthesized answer from memories

post.description:
Surface relevant memories, decisions, intentions, and warnings.

Runs the full proactive recall pipeline: retrieve → rank → rerank
→ anti-annoyance filtering → categorize.

With ``index_only``, returns a compact index instead of the four
populated buckets and records nothing — no cooldown, no access count.
Expand what you want via ``POST /api/v1/memories/batch``, which is where
that bookkeeping then happens.

Surface up to 2 relevant memories for a mid-session event.

Lighter than session-start recall — fewer candidates, smaller
result set, respects session surface cap.

``index_only`` behaves as it does at session start: compact lines, and
no surfacing recorded until the caller expands.

ApproveBody.description:
Optional extras when keeping a memory.

``confirm_as_owner_fact`` is the owner saying, of a memory that came from
outside — a page an agent read, an email, an external MCP write — "yes,
this is my own fact": the one way such content reaches the always-loaded
profile card (core/evidence.py, learn-only-from-owner). It defaults to
off, so an ordinary approve keeps a memory usable without ever promoting
outside text to the owner's word.

Setting it needs an owner-authenticated ingress — a paired phone's own
token, or a key the deployment named as the owner's. Anyone else asking
for it gets 403 rather than a quiet downgrade: a caller that believes it
is confirming an owner fact should be told it is not.
ApproveBody.title: ApproveBody

answered.description: False when the retrieved memories did not answer the question and the model said so. Search always returns rows and no ranking signal separates a real hit from the closest of a bad lot (see evals/score-separability.md), so this is the only honest 'I don't know' the API offers — act on it rather than on `score`.

MemoryIndexItem.description:
One line of a progressive-disclosure index.

The compact half of the recall contract: enough for a model to decide
whether it wants a memory, not enough to be the memory. ``content`` is
truncated; expand via ``POST /api/v1/memories/batch`` to get the full
:class:`MemoryResponse`.

``status`` is carried deliberately rather than dropped as bookkeeping —
it is the only handle callers (and the approval-gate tests) have on
whether an item is ``active`` or ``pending``.
MemoryIndexItem.title: MemoryIndexItem

MemoryResponse.description: Serialized memory returned by the API.

score.description: Relevance of this memory to the query that returned it, when it came from a search. None on every other path, where there is no query to be relevant to. ORDINAL, NOT CALIBRATED: it is the hybrid ranker's weighted sum of cosine similarity and ts_rank, so it orders results honestly but 0.6 means nothing on its own. Compare scores within one response; derive any threshold from measurement (see evals/) rather than picking a round number.
score.title: Score

Off by default so existing callers keep the shape they parse today. Expand the ids you actually want via POST /api/v1/memories/batch, which is also where the recall cooldown and access count are recorded.

In index mode the link is written at the expand step, like the cooldown.

include_pending.description: Opt-in: also include 'pending' (unapproved) memories. Off by default so agent/automation callers (e.g. the MCP search tool) never see unapproved content; the dashboard sets this explicitly to show pending items (badged).
include_pending.title: Include Pending

include_trail.description: Opt-in: also search the raw capture trail and return matching passages in `trail`. Extraction is lossy — the sentence a fact came from often answers a question the fact no longer can. Off by default so existing callers keep the shape they parse today.

index_only.description: Opt-in: return a compact index (id, truncated content, tags, score, status) instead of full memory objects, roughly a tenth of the tokens. Off by default so existing callers keep the shape they parse today; a model-facing caller should set it and expand the few ids it actually needs via POST /api/v1/memories/batch.

search_mode.description: Search strategy: 'vector' (cosine only), 'hybrid' (vector+BM25), 'tri_hybrid' (vector+BM25+graph), 'judged' (hybrid's candidates kept and ordered by the local relevance judge; may return none when nothing fits)
